claim:
Text: "Joe Biden wants to ban fracking"
Claim author: The Donald Trump 2020 presidential campaign
Claim date: October 27, 2020
before_justification: The final verdict refutes the claim based on clear, consistent evidence that Joe Biden explicitly and repeatedly stated during his 2020 presidential campaign that he would not ban fracking, declaring in a speech, “I am not banning fracking. Let me say that again. I am not banning fracking” ([source](https://energynow.com/2020/09/the-biden-flip-flop-u-s-presidential-hopeful-biden-now-says-he-would-not-ban-fracking/)). His official campaign platform did not include a nationwide fracking ban, though it proposed ending new oil and gas leasing on federal lands and transitioning away from fossil fuels ([source](https://www.newsweek.com/fact-check-does-joe-biden-support-green-new-deal-fracking-ban-1537291)). The Trump campaign’s claim was characterized as misleading, as it relied on decontextualized statements to misrepresent Biden’s position ([source](https://apnews.com/article/election-2020-joe-biden-donald-trump-pennsylvania-elections-c28fbf9d921915f3a65c01e6c4cebcf6)).
after_justification: The fact-check found contradictory evidence regarding Joe Biden's official policy stance on fracking during the 2020 campaign. Direct quotes and reporting from [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/graphics/USA-ELECTION/POLICY/ygdpzwarjvw//created) indicate he proposed banning new oil and gas leasing on federal lands while stating he would "not ban fracking" overall. However, other cited sources, including summaries from the [American Bar Association](https://www.americanbar.org/groups/crsj/publications/human_rights_magazine_home/voting-in-2020/political-advertising-on-social-media-platforms//created) and [CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/texas/news/north-texas-city-that-banned-fracking-pushes-back-in-court//created), assert his official campaign platform called for a "complete and immediate nationwide ban on all hydraulic fracturing." The record does not contain a single, unambiguous piece of evidence—such as a direct citation from the official campaign document—to conclusively resolve this inconsistency, leading to the verdict of `refuted` based on the unclear and conflicting evidence.

Hydraulic fracturing is a technique in which large volumes of water and sand, and small volumes of chemical additives are injected into low-permeability subsurface formations to increase oil or natural gas flow.
The injection pressure of the pumped fluid creates fractures that enhance gas and fluid flow, and the sand or other coarse material holds the fractures open.
Most of the injected fluid flows back to the wellbore and is pumped to the surface.
Hydraulic fracturing has been used for over 60 years in over one million wells. Recently, public concern about potential impacts on drinking water and other environmental damage has significantly grown.
Consequently, Congress directed the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) in 2010 to conduct a study of this practice to better understand any potential impacts of hydraulic fracturing on drinking water and groundwater.
DOE/NETL is working closely with the EPA as it carries out the study and is also collaborating with the Department of the Interior to enhance understanding of these risks.
On May 5, 2011, U.S. Energy Secretary Steven Chu charged the Secretary of Energy Advisory Board (SEAB) Natural Gas Subcommittee to make recommendations to improve the safety and environmental performance of natural gas hydraulic fracturing from shale formations.
Secretary Chu extended the Subcommittee membership beyond SEAB members to include the natural gas industry, states, and environmental experts.
The Subcommittee is supported by the Departments of Energy and Interior, and the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency.
President Obama directed U.S. Energy Secretary Chu to form the Natural Gas Subcommittee as part of the President’s "Blueprint for a Secure Energy Future" - a comprehensive plan to reduce America's oil dependence, save consumers money, and make our country the leader in clean energy industries.
